newsitem.title: UK: CRESTCo proposes higher user fees to fund upgrades.
newsitem.headline: CRESTCo proposes higher user fees to fund upgrades.

text.p: CRESTCo, the Bank of England-led the group that operates the London Stock Exchange's electronic share settlement system, said it had proposed raising user fees to pay for upgrades.

CRESTCo's board of directors has already approved tariff increases that would add three million stg, or about 15 percent, to the group's annual revenue of roughly 20 million stg, CRESTCo manager Paul Symons said.
He said the CRESTCo board is waiting for feedback from the industry before putting the new structure in place and setting an implementation date.

"The market has a clear choice. People can say "we're perfectly happy to have slow turnaround time on files and have low tariffs'," Symons told Reuters. "But if the market wants quick turnaround time, the they'll have to pay for it."
CRESTCo recently installed upgrades that will have bolstered the processing capacity of Crest by 60 percent when it goes live later this month ahead of "bed and breakfast" season.
The group is considering buying new computers at the end of 1997 to upgrade the entire system at a cost of some 2.5 million stg, Symons said.
The revenue generated by the proposed tariff hikes would finance the upgrades and the fee structure would not be reviewed again in 1997, he said.
Some services that previously were free, like inputting messages and files into the system, will carry a 2p charge per input.
CRESTCo also proposed charging for resubmission of trades for settlement after their intended settlement date.
Some changes were introduced specifically to finance additional capacity, while others were introduced to influence when and how the system is used.

Asked whether fees might be raised again in 1998, Symons said: "This year is the most important year as far as capacity goes. We've got the general election, which always means more trading, and six building societies converting. The big strain on capacity will be this year, not next year."
